==English==
{{wp}}
[[File:Hexahedron.svg|thumb|A cube]]

===Etymology 1===
From {{uder|en|fro|cube|}}, from {{uder|en|la|cubus}}, from {{uder|en|grc|κύβος|}}.

{{displaced|ang|tæfel}} ("cube, die, game with dice or tables").

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|kyo͞ob|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/kjuːb/}}
* {{enPR|kyo͞ob|a=US}}, {{IPA|en|/kjub/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-cube.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|uːb|s=1}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|geometry}} A [[regular]] [[polyhedron]] having six identical square faces.
#: {{ux|en|When the math teacher is teaching the class about '''cubes''', he asks them to imagine a cardboard box whose width, length, and height are all the same.}}
# Any object more or less in the form of a cube.
#: {{hypo|en|sugar cube|stock cube}}
#: {{ux|en|A: One '''cube''' or two? B: Oh, no sugar for me, thanks.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q861555}} {{lb|en|mathematics}} The third [[power]] of a [[number]], [[value]], [[term]] or expression.
#: {{ant|en|cube root<id:Q1774143>}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''cube''' of 2 is 8.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''cube''' of 0.5 is 0.125.}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} A [[data structure]] consisting of a [[three-dimensional]] [[array]]; a [[data cube]].
# A {{w|Rubik's cube}} style puzzle, not necessarily in the shape of a cube.
# {{senseid|en|Q2140397}} {{lb|en|informal|automotive}} {{clipping of|en|cubic inch<id:Q2140397><alt:cubic inch(es)>}}.
#: {{ux|en|As if the 383 weren't already a roaring beast, in 1972 they bored it out some more, bringing it up to 400 '''cubes'''. This 400-'''cube''' monster could launch a land yacht like the Plymouth Fury from zero to sixty in under ten seconds.}}
# {{senseid|en|uncool person}} {{lb|en|1950s|_|slang|dated}} An extremely socially [[conventional]] or [[conservative]] person, more so than even a [[square]].

Uncertain.
